name: Avi Srivastava
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Avi is an Assistant Professor at The Wistar Institute in Philadelphia. He is a computational biologist by training and by temperament — his research sits at the intersection of statistical machine learning, high-performance algorithms, and modern functional genomics. Across his career, Avi has built methods and tools that the single-cell community now uses every day: from the salmon / alevin / alevin-fry lineage of quantification tools, to multimodal integration frameworks underlying Signac and Seurat v5, to the scCUT&Tag-pro assay-and-analysis pair for single-cell chromatin states. His work has appeared in Nature Methods, Nature Biotechnology, Cell, Genome Biology, Bioinformatics, and Nature Reviews Genetics. Before joining Wistar, Avi was a postdoctoral fellow with Rahul Satija at the New York Genome Center and NYU. He earned his Ph.D. in Computer Science at Stony Brook University, advised by Rob Patro.
